questions.subject: Physics
questions.question: Rolling friction is very much smaller than sliding friction. This is the reason why:
options: Brakes do not work on wheels
Ball bearings and wheels are used to move heavy loads easily
questions.explanation: Rolling replaces sliding contact with a continuously changing point of contact, so much less deformation and resistance occur. The invention of the wheel rests on this fact.
questions.ncertReference: Physics Class 11, Chapter 4: Laws of Motion

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question: For a sustained interference pattern to be observed, the two sources of light must be:
options: Coherent, that is they must maintain a constant phase difference
questions.explanation: Two independent lamps cannot interfere because their phase difference changes randomly, which is why Young split a single beam into two with a double slit.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question: In an intrinsic semiconductor at a temperature above absolute zero:
options: The number of free electrons equals the number of holes
questions.explanation: Every electron that jumps the gap to the conduction band leaves exactly one hole behind, so ne = nh. Doping is what breaks this equality and gives n-type or p-type material.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question: The percentage by mass of nitrogen in ammonia, NH₃, is approximately (N = 14, H = 1):
questions.explanation: Molar mass is 14 + 3 = 17, so the mass percentage of nitrogen is (14/17) × 100, about 82 percent. This high nitrogen content is why ammonia based fertilisers are so valuable.
questions.ncertReference: Chemistry Class 11, Chapter 1: Some Basic Concepts of Chemistry

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question: According to Saytzeff's rule, the dehydrohalogenation of 2-bromobutane with alcoholic KOH gives mainly:
options: But-2-ene, the more substituted and more stable alkene
questions.explanation: The hydrogen is removed from the carbon with fewer hydrogens, which yields the alkene stabilised by more hyperconjugation. With aqueous KOH, substitution would give the alcohol instead.
questions.ncertReference: Chemistry Class 12, Chapter 6: Haloalkanes and Haloarenes

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question: The metal ion present at the centre of the chlorophyll molecule and that in haemoglobin are respectively:
questions.explanation: Both are coordination compounds with a porphyrin type ring. Vitamin B12 is a cobalt complex, and carbonic anhydrase contains zinc.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question: RuBisCO is often described as the most abundant protein in the whole biosphere because it:
options: Is present in the blood of all animals
Is present in enormous amounts in the chloroplasts of every green plant
questions.explanation: It is a slow and inefficient enzyme, so plants must make vast quantities of it to fix enough carbon, and it can make up half the soluble protein of a leaf.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question: Cryopreservation of gametes and seeds in liquid nitrogen is a method of:
questions.explanation: Ex-situ methods keep the organism or its propagules away from their natural habitat, as in seed banks, zoos, botanical gardens and tissue culture collections.
questions.ncertReference: Biology Class 12, Chapter 13: Biodiversity and Conservation

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.question: Osteoporosis, a common age related skeletal disorder, involves:
options: An excess of calcium in the bones
A decrease in bone mass and mineral content, often linked to low oestrogen levels
Accumulation of uric acid in joints
questions.explanation: The bones become porous and fracture easily, and the risk rises sharply in women after menopause. Gout is the uric acid disorder and myasthenia gravis the junction disorder.
questions.ncertReference: Biology Class 11, Chapter 17: Locomotion and Movement

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.question: In the assisted reproductive technique called GIFT, what is transferred and to where?
options: An ovum from a donor into the fallopian tube of a woman who cannot produce one
questions.explanation: GIFT stands for gamete intrafallopian transfer. It suits a woman who cannot produce an ovum but can provide a suitable environment for fertilisation and further development.
